hypotheses.name: H1 break-even target after X hours
hypotheses.rationale: Of the 2021-23 trades still open X hours after the fill, many trade back up to the entry price and then fall into the 48h time stop. So once a position is X hours old, the +1.5% take-profit limit is lowered to entry +0.2% (break-even after fees) or entry +0.5%. Same fill rules as the take-profit: an open already above the target sells at the open, otherwise the high must trade 0.1% through. The change is made at the hourly cycle after hour X closes.

hypotheses.name: H2 stale-loser exit at hour X
hypotheses.rationale: In 2021-23, positions 3-10% under water 18-30h after the fill mostly kept sliding into the time stop. Positions more than 10% under water were in a fresh panic and bounced, which is the bot's own thesis. So the bot checks once, at the close of the X-th hour after the fill hour. If entry*(1-sd) < close <= entry*(1-su), it sells at market (close x (1-slip), the same convention as the time stop). sd = none means a plain 'under water' exit. A hard stop-loss from entry was not gridded because the 2021-23 data argued against it at every level.

Findings:
(1) A hard stop-loss from entry is unsupported even in 2021-23. At hourly closes from -5% to -20%, the stopped trades would on net have done better if held, because deep losers are fresh panics that bounce. It was therefore not gridded.
(2) What happens to time-stop losers depends on the market regime. (3) A break-even target turns future +1.5% winners into +0.3% exits. In 2024-26 the pick made 151 break-even exits at +0.3% while time stops only fell from 67 to 48, so all 8 variants were below live there (x2.49-2.58).

The lens's premise holds in-sample: the time-stop losers can be cut in 2021-23. It does not carry over to 2024-26, where the cut losers would mostly have recovered.

result.lens: entry: avoid buys likely to become time-stop losers (filters computed at the hour the order is placed, closed candles only)

hypotheses.name: H1 knife filter: coin already falling before the dip AND most of the market weak -> skip (smult=0) or 16% trigger
hypotheses.rationale: The edge is a liquidation overshoot in an otherwise healthy market. A coin that was already sliding for days before the current 24h dip, inside a broad sell-off, is more likely being repriced, and a 48h hold doesn't survive that. Flag = pre3d (close[t-25]/close[t-97]-1) <= -a AND breadth (share of live coins whose last close is under their 7-day average close) >= b. Grid: thresholds a in {0,3,6}% and b in {0.80,0.90,0.95}, with action skip or 16% depth.
hypotheses.motivation_evidence_2021_23: All from the 1,681 live-setting trades bought in 2021-23 (r2_entry_analysis*.py; no 2024-26 numbers printed before the grids ran). Breadth7 was the strongest single separator (AUC 0.613 for time stop; breadth > 0.938: 579 trades, 10.2% time stops, avg +0.25%, vs 2.9% and +1.95% when breadth <= 0.31). Coin downtrend before the dip: pre3d <= -3% averaged +0.58% (2021) / +0.31% (2022-23), against +1.54% / +0.96% otherwise. The joint 'knife' flag (pre3d <= -3% and breadth >= 0.9), 455 trades on 119 buy days, averaged +0.01% (2021, 11.3% time stops, contrib -0.26) and +0.15% (2022-23, 9.8%, contrib +0.05). The rest averaged +1.57%/+0.96%. The flag also caught the worst clusters: 2021-05-21 (breadth 1.0, r3d -26%), 2022-06-13 (breadth 1.0), 2021-12-04, 2022-01-21 and 2022-08-19. Features with no separation: volume surge (qv24/qv4 vs 30d, AUC 0.50), BTC 24h drop (0.50), BTC 30d-high distance (0.50), hours since the 24h high, a recent time stop on the same coin (AUC 0.49, slightly fewer time stops after one), idiosyncratic vs market drop, number of coins near trigger.

result.key_findings:
1. In 2021-23, time-stop losers can be predicted from information available when the order is placed. Market breadth (share of coins below their 7-day average) and the coin's own slide before the dip were the strongest signals. Volume surges, BTC's 24h drop, distance from the 30-day high and a recent time stop on the same coin added nothing. The 'knife' set (pre3d <= -3% and breadth >= 0.9) was 27% of 2021-23 trades and averaged about 0% (+0.01% in 2021, +0.15% in 2022-23), with roughly double the time-stop rate.
2. Skipping those buys transforms 2021-23: the H1 pick goes to x6.19 with a -15% worst drop (live x5.75, -29%), and 7 of 8 variants beat live there. It does not carry over. In 2024-26 all 8 variants are lower (x1.92-x2.33 vs x2.61) and the worst drop doesn't improve (-16%, two variants -12%). The post-hoc split (r2_entry_posthoc.py, run after both grids) shows why. In 2024-26 the flagged trades were as good as the rest: knife pre<=-3% br>=0.80 averaged +0.95% with 8.2% time stops (343 trades) vs +1.17% and 7.2% unflagged. knife br>=0.90 averaged +1.00% with 6.9% time stops vs +1.13% and 7.9%. r1h>0 averaged +1.25% with 6.9% time stops vs +1.05% and 7.7%. The worst subgroup in 2021-23 (r1h>0 & knife, -1.51% avg, 18.8% time stops) had 0 time stops in 2024-26 (44 trades, +1.38%). The 2021-23 pattern was a bear-market and 2021-crash effect: losses in sustained broad sell-offs, which 2024-26 barely had.
3. Both hypotheses rejected (16 variants run, each grid once): H1 pick 2024-26 x2.06, H2 pick 2024-26 x2.60 vs x2.61. Both also fail the LUNA/FTT/SRM and fills-0.2%-worse checks. Live bot unchanged.
4. Takeaway for future entry filters: the time-stop losers in 2021-23 cluster in broad bear phases. Filters that cut them sharply lower 2021-23 drawdowns, but they give up 2024-26 return because the same conditions produced normal winners there. The 2024-26 worst drop (-16%) did not come from knife-type buys.

hypotheses.name: H1 extra leg 2, funded first from free cash
hypotheses.rationale: The damage in a market-wide cascade sits in the first fills, which keep falling, and averaging down is what rescues them. The first leg stays exactly as live (12% trigger, 8 closest coins, cap 20%). From the hourly cycle after the first leg fills, a fully funded limit buy of x times the first leg's money rests at ref_fill*(1-d2), where ref_fill is the 24h high that set the trigger. If the hour's open is already under that level, it buys at market. These leg-2 orders are funded first from free cash (all scaled down together if cash is short); the rest of the cash goes to the usual first-leg orders. Unfilled leg-2 orders are cancelled and re-placed each hour. After leg 2 fills, the take-profit is the average cost x 1.015, placed at the next cycle (none in the leg-2 fill hour). The 48h time stop and 24h cooldown count from the first fill. Grid, fixed before any run: x in {0.5, 1.0} x d2 in {16, 18, 20, 24%} = 8 variants. Custom kernel ckernel (a copy of gkernel). With the ladder off it is bit-identical to engine.run: x5.75 / x2.61, and also with dead coins x5.29 / x2.46, fills 0.2% worse x3.98 / x2.37, and both x3.63 / x2.24. It also passes 5 hand-made one-coin path checks.

hypotheses.name: H2 split ladder on fewer coins
hypotheses.rationale: This is the textbook ladder: each selected coin's budget is split, w at the 12% trigger and 1-w at ref*(1-d2), both resting from the hour start, so both can fill in the same hour. After the first leg fills, leg 2 keeps resting at that fixed price with its cash locked until it fills or the position is sold. The same exit rules as H1 apply. On 2021-23 data a split on the live 8 coins lowered the crude per-trade total in all 8 combinations (+3.70 to +4.28 vs +4.75 live), because half the first-leg money sits idle in the 70-90% of trades that never reach leg 2. So the first leg keeps about the live size by using fewer coins: w=1/2 on 4 coins and w=2/3 on 5 coins, with cap fmax = 20%/w per coin (so a coin's two legs can total 40% / 30% of equity). Grid, fixed before any run: 2 (w, N) x d2 in {16, 18, 20, 24%} = 8 variants. Same ckernel and equivalence proof as H1.

result.key_findings:
Neither crowding rule passes, so the live bot stays unchanged. Each grid ran once through study.study(), with engine.run pointed at my kernel copy in memory. That kernel, with its switches off, is bit-identical to engine.run (x5.75 / x2.61).

(1) Capping fills per hour is not worth testing, because the 2021-23 data points the other way. Inside crowded hours the first fills are the ones that keep falling: ranks 1-2 average -0.07% with 13.4% time stops. The late fills are the best trades: ranks 5-6 +1.57%, ranks 7-8 +1.82%. A cap that cancels resting buys after F fills would skip trades averaging +1.08% to +1.82% while keeping ones averaging +0.94% to +0.97%. Rolling 6/12/24h caps show no damage either. The fill order comes from 1-minute data (r2_crowding_fm.py, 0.00% mismatch with the hourly fills).

(2) Averaging down does help. A second leg returns +2.3% to +5.0% on its own money on exactly the losing first legs. In the backtest:
- H2 (split ladder, 50% at 12% / 50% at 18% on the 4 closest coins) beats live in both periods: x9.07 / -23% in 2021-23 and x2.67 / -15% in 2024-26. It also beats live with fills 0.2% worse (x7.56 / x2.49). It fails the LUNA/FTT/SRM check (21-23 x4.96 with a -49% drop; 24-26 x2.35 vs x2.46). The cause is concentration: the 40% per-coin cap let one LUNA trade in May 2021 take 40% of equity and lose 47.4%.

LENS realism: 1-minute candles, live settings, 19 coins. No strategy change and no pick. The baseline is the 1-minute engine: 2021-23 x5.74, worst drop -29%, 2022 +19%; 2024-26 x2.61, worst drop -16%.

(a) Anatomy of the live limit-buy fills (2021-23 / 2024-26)
- Count: 1,506 / 826 resting limit fills, plus 175 / 58 market buys at the hour open.
- Fill minute: median minute 26 of the hour. Only 28 (1.9%) / 13 (1.6%) fills happen in minute 0, before the bot's orders are really up.
- How far through the limit the price traded (lowest low from the fill to the hour end): median 1.25% / 1.05%, 10th percentile 0.25% / 0.25%.
  - Less than 0.3% through: 12.5% / 13.4% of fills.
  - Less than 0.5% through: 22.2% / 25.9%.
  - Less than 1% through: 42.2% / 47.7%.
- How long the price stayed at or below the limit:
  - Consecutive minutes with the low at or below the limit, in the run holding the fill minute: median 4 / 4. Under 2 minutes: 16.5% / 15.3%. Under 5 minutes: 52.1% / 54.5%.
  - Longest run of minute closes at or below the limit: under 2 minutes for 27.1% / 29.4%, under 5 minutes for 47.9% / 49.8%.
  - Minutes in the hour with the low at or below the limit: median 11 / 9.
- The shallow fills are the best trades:
  - 0-0.2% through: 96 fills averaging +1.76% (2021-23); 60 fills averaging +1.23% (2024-26).
  - 0.2-0.3% through: +1.87% / +1.41%.
  - 5% or more through: 143 fills averaging -1.43% with 29 time stops (2021-23); 77 fills averaging -0.49% (2024-26).
- So every stricter rule removes winners. Fills dropped on the live path (counted against the same live trades, without re-running):
  - 0.3% through: 189 fills averaging +1.81%, against +0.83% for the kept fills (2021-23); 111 averaging +1.32%, against +1.04% kept (2024-26).
  - Low at or below the limit for 2 or more minutes: 139 averaging +2.23% (2021-23); 80 averaging +2.09% (2024-26).

critic.overall_assessment:
The live bot's settings should stay as they are. Round 2's work is sound: I found no rule violations, no lookahead and no number mismatches, and all 8 picks fail the rule. A cleaner +LUNA/FTT/SRM check does not rescue any of them. But the round left two problems that matter more than any refinement. First, the live bot as coded is not the strategy that was backtested. Second, the dead-coin robustness check is partly an artifact.

What I checked:
- Read every r2_*.py. All four custom kernels are line-by-line copies of gkernel/mkernel, and each one's equivalence proof passes in its log. The new features look only at the past: shift(1) or older, and refs are 24h closes shifted by 1. Stale/time-stop exits sell at the hour's close, the same as the existing time stop. The motivation scripts filter to before 2024.
- Reran r2_crowding.py, r2_entry_h2_cascade.py and r2_losers.py into pb_out_r2/critic/. Every number is identical to the reports, including the split pick (2021-23 x9.07 / -23%, 2024-26 x2.67, +dead x4.96 / -49%, 0.2%-worse fills x7.56 / x2.49) and the entry H2 near miss (2024-26 x2.5985). The agents' own logs for entry H1 and trigger H1/H2 match their summaries.
- The crowding claim that one LUNA trade was "40% of equity" is real. With fmax=0.4 it happens when only 1-2 coins are free to buy because the rest are held or cooling down.
- Rebuilt realism row (f) on hourly candles with a new kernel (r2_critic_f.py; with its switches off it gives exactly the engine.run results). It gives 2021-23 x4.73 / 2024-26 x2.66, against the realism agent's 1-minute x4.72 / x2.66. The cause is confirmed in panic_buyer.py: open_position() calls place_tp() right after a market buy, so the +1.5% sell goes up inside the buy hour. And because opened_ms is the start of the buy hour, the 48h time stop fires one hour earlier than the backtest's.

What matters for the live bot:
1. The bot as coded backtests at x4.7 in 2021-23, not the advertised x5.75. Market buys in 2021-23 average +0.1% instead of +1.2%. The comparison is mixed. Backtest timing wins in 2021-23 (x5.75 vs x4.73), and with 0.2%-worse fills (x3.98 vs x3.38). Live timing wins slightly in 2024-26 (x2.66 vs x2.61), and with LUNA/FTT/SRM added (x5.69 vs x5.29, though with a -34% vs -31% drop). Neither version beats the other on every test. This is an implementation choice for the user, not a refinement that passed the rule.
2. The split ladder (half at 12%, half at 18%, 4 coins) is the only real near miss. It is the only variant that beat live in both periods, and it survives 0.2%-worse fills. It fails only on concentration: up to 40% of equity can sit in one coin. A capped version has to be treated as a new, post-hoc hypothesis, because this ladder family has already been checked against 2024-26.

The other results are best read as in-sample effects. Cutting stale losers and filtering knife-catching entries improve 2021-23 drawdowns a lot (-15% to -24%), but the effect vanishes in 2024-26 because it came from bear-market conditions.

- Motivation: the scripts restrict to trades that exited, or for entry were bought, before 2024. Entry's "bought before 2024" can include up to 48h of January 2024 prices, which is negligible.
- Pre-run fixes: entry's breadth-liveness change and crowding's synthetic test data were fixed before the grids ran. Both are disclosed.

Soft issues, not violations:
(a) The agents had read REFINE.md and HANDOFF.md, which show 2024-26 results for related ideas, e.g. that fewer and larger orders and shorter cooldowns raise both return and drawdown. Lens choice was therefore not fully blind. About 16 picks across two rounds have now been checked against 2024-26, so it is no longer a clean holdout.
(b) Crowding H2 used fmax = 20%/w. That breaks the live 20% per-coin cap by design, and it is exactly why the pick failed.

I found no mismatches. My reruns gave identical numbers:
- crowding H1 pick: x7.51 / x2.37
- crowding H2 pick: x9.07 / x2.67; +dead x4.96 / -49% / x2.35; 0.2%-worse fills x7.56 / x2.49
- entry H2 pick: x6.26 / 2.5985; +dead x5.38 / -33% / x2.45; 0.2%-worse fills x2.37
- losers H1 pick: x6.35 / x2.55
- losers H2 pick: x6.62 / x2.19
- all 16 losers rows

Realism (f) was reproduced independently on hourly candles: x4.73 / x2.66 against x4.72 / x2.66. Trade anatomy matches the brief: 1,681 / 884 trades, time stops 108 / 67, take-profit sums +9.84 / +14.44 and time-stop sums -5.09 / -5.18. Minor wording: the losers script docstring says "+0.76 at h24", which is the sum of the two bins reported (+0.338 and +0.419).

One existing-engine artifact, not an agent error, distorts the +LUNA/FTT/SRM check. The FTT hourly data ends at 2022-11-15 04:00, but the cut in engine.DEAD is 2023-09-22. In that last candle the live bot market-buys FTT (open 1.4228, trigger 1.490). The position never exits, so its money stays stuck at the last FTT price for the rest of the run. Dropping that single hour changes the +dead live baseline from x5.29 / x2.46 to x5.48 / x2.61. That x2.46 is also the HANDOFF's "RM14,753 with collapses" figure for 2024-26. Re-measuring all 8 picks without that hour flips no verdict to a pass. Trigger H1's +dead leg goes from ok to FAILS (x2.54 vs x2.61); it had already failed the 0.2%-worse fill check. Crowding H2's 2024-26 +dead result becomes x2.67, which beats live, but its 2021-23 -49% drop (May 2021) still fails.
missing: The live bot as coded differs from the validated backtest for market buys (realism row f, independently confirmed by r2_critic_f.py). The bot places the +1.5% sell immediately and counts 48h from the start of the buy hour, so it backtests at 2021-23 x4.73 vs x5.75. All round-2 variants were compared against the backtest timing, not the bot's actual behavior, and nobody tested which timing to adopt under the rule.

The +LUNA/FTT/SRM check has an artifact. A position still open when a coin's data ends stays valued at that coin's last price forever, and its money never comes back. The FTT market buy in the final FTT hour (2022-11-15 04:00) drives the 2024-26 leg of this check (live x2.46 vs x2.61 without that hour). engine.DEAD's FTT cut date (2023-09-22) also doesn't match where the data ends. No agent noticed it.

Split ladder with both legs capped at 20-25% of equity per coin: the obvious follow-up to the only variant that beat live in both periods. It is not tested. Because the ladder family has already been checked against 2024-26, it would need a pre-registered grid and an untouched holdout (a forward/paper run, or coins from univ/ outside the 19).

How market buys are handled (coin already under its trigger at the open: 175 / 58 trades) was never a hypothesis: e.g. TP timing, or a limit order at the trigger instead of a market buy. Row f shows this choice is worth about ±18% of the 2021-23 multiple.

Not independently verified by me: the realism 1-minute fill anatomy (fill-depth distribution, minute-0 fills, rows b-e/g/h); entry's 2024-26 post-hoc split; the crowding fill-rank analysis from 1-minute data (r2_crowding_fm.py); the trigger single-coin bot statistics; the losers motivation tables. The synthetic unit tests were only read, not rerun.
No uncertainty estimate on near misses. Gaps like x2.5985 vs x2.6088 (entry H2) or x2.6139 (trigger 16h) are far inside block-bootstrap noise. Without one, 'near miss' versus 'tie' is not meaningful.

Untested exit and entry ideas outside the rejected list: a take-profit relative to the 24h high (sell at a fraction of the way back to it) instead of a fixed +1.5%; time-of-day / weekend effects on entry quality (liquidations cluster in thin hours).
recommended_next: Have the user decide market-buy handling explicitly. Option 1: align panic_buyer.py with the validated backtest (for market buys, place the take-profit at the next cycle via manage_positions, and count 48h from the end of the buy hour). Option 2: re-baseline the backtest to the bot's real behavior and expect about x4.7 (2021-23) / x2.66 (2024-26). In either case, reconcile_live.py should log market-buy trades separately.

Fix the dead-coin convention before any further robustness checks. Force-close a position at the coin's last candle (at its last close minus a haircut, or at -100% for LUNA-type collapses), and set engine.DEAD's FTT cut to where the FTT data actually ends. Then rerun the live baseline +dead numbers in REFINE.md and HANDOFF.md, since x2.46 / RM14,753 is an artifact.

If the split ladder is pursued: pre-register at most 8 variants with the total per coin capped at 20-25% of equity (e.g. w 0.5/0.67 x d2 16/18/20% with N=4/5). Pick on 2021-23, and validate on data the round hasn't seen: forward paper trading from Nov 2026, or a top-20 to top-50 coin set from univ/ that excludes the 19. Don't count another 2024-26 check as out of sample.
Add a block-bootstrap (for example 3-month blocks) confidence band on the 2024-26 multiple and drawdown differences versus live, so near misses can be judged against noise.

Keep the live strategy settings unchanged. Use the realism range (2021-23 x3.3-4.7, 2024-26 x2.35-2.66) as the expectation for the bot as coded, and compare the first 2-4 live weeks to it with reconcile_live.py.
